ws1.broken_count: 9 sites examined. 3 broken on PE (#3 arena reserve — misses -1, latent; #5 rt_veh — no OOM handling at all, crashes, the likely cause of the tester's crash; #6 string + — check skipped entirely on PE). 1 touch-time class (#2/#4/#7's caveat — any arena allocation that touches a new page under a commit limit crashes via #5, even though the allocation check itself works — this is really #5, not a separate site, but it is the mechanism by which the tester's crash happens). 4 work on PE (#1 growth region, #4 nirmmita mmap fallback, #7 kosh make, #9 region allocator). 1 allocates nothing (#8 FFI). So it is a CLASS, and it needs a gate.
ws1.root_cause: The PE allocation shim returns -1 (Linux MAP_FAILED convention) on failure, but the compiler's allocation-failure checks test only for 0 (NULL) — and, separately, the arena's lazy page-commit on Windows (rt_veh) has no OOM handling at all, so a commit failure crashes instead of refusing. On Linux, the mmap paths normalise -errno to 0, so the checks work; on PE, there is no normalisation in the paths that matter, so -1 slips through (or the failure happens at touch time, where there is no check at all). Evidence: win/winrt_blob.asm:183, .error: mov rax,-1 (the shared error path for .alloc/.free/.close — on PE, a failed VirtualAlloc returns -1, not 0). r127_emit_grow_check (src/sutram_compiler.asm:21254) emits test rax,rax; jnz ok — if rax != 0 it thinks the allocation succeeded; if rax == -1 (PE shim failure), jnz ok is taken (because -1 != 0) and the code proceeds to use -1 as a buffer pointer, writing to an invalid address -> 0xC0000005, with no message printed (because the failure path, which prints the message, is never reached — hence empty output, matching the tester's table). On Linux, the mmap paths normalise -errno to 0 (emit_nirmmita_from_rax: 'mmap reports failure as -errno (-4095..-1), and nirmmita promises 0 on failure. Map the error range to 0'; r101a_a2: cmp rax,-4095; jb +2; xor eax,eax — the same mapping), so the check catches it (refuses with the message, exit 1). On PE, the region path ALSO has this normalisation (the emitted r101a_a2 bytes run on the target, and -1 is in [-4095,-1], so it maps to 0 there too) — so the region path should refuse on PE as well, not crash. Which means the tester's crash is NOT (primarily) in the region mmap — it is in a path that has NO normalisation and NO check (the arena / rt_veh, site #5). The region path is fixed; the crash is elsewhere.

sites.check: No — no OOM handling at all. On VirtualAlloc failure (returns NULL, 0), it jumps to .v_search, which returns EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH (0) — 'I didn't handle this, keep searching' — and if no other handler handles it, the process dies with an unhandled access violation (0xC0000005).
sites.name: Arena page-commit (rt_veh, the vectored exception handler, win/winrt_blob.asm:240-280)
sites.via: VirtualAlloc (MEM_COMMIT, up to 64 KiB) to commit a page when it is first touched
sites.works_on_pe: No — this is the crash. This is the likely cause of the tester's Windows OOM crash: the growth (via the arena, in-place extend or bump) touches a new page, the commit fails under the commit limit, rt_veh returns CONTINUE_SEARCH, and the program dies with 0xC0000005 and empty output (no message, because the crash happens in the middle of the growth/touch, before any OOM check can run). This is a CLASS, not a single site: any arena allocation that touches a new page under a commit limit will crash, not refuse — including kosh growth (arena path), nirmmita (arena bump), and string + (via nirmmita arena). On Linux there is no rt_veh (Linux uses MAP_NORESERVE + overcommit, and the OOM is caught at allocation time (mmap fails, normalised to 0, grow check refuses) BEFORE the page is touched). So Linux refuses, Windows crashes — because on Windows the failure happens at TOUCH time (page commit, no handling), not at ALLOCATION time (mmap/VirtualAlloc, which has handling).

ws2.linux_verified: Yes — refuses on Linux (verified by me). No limit: prints 10000001, exit 0 (succeeds, as expected — 80 MB fits). Under ulimit -v 65536 (64 MB): prints exactly one line — 'Sutram truti: kosh vardhayitum smritih na labdha - kosh yatha asit tatha eva' — exit 1. So it refuses on Linux, quickly, with the grow message.
ws2.needs_commit_limit_on_windows: Yes — the Windows defect needs a specific commit limit to appear (in the sense that, without one, there is enough memory, so no OOM, so no crash): at 2048 MiB it works (exit 0), at 256 MiB or less it crashes. So the test must set a commit limit (e.g. 64 MiB, as in the tester's table and as in my Linux ulimit test) for the crash to appear; on a machine with plenty of memory, the program works (exit 0) and the defect is invisible. That changes how it gets tested: the gate must run under a commit limit (a Windows Job with a per-process commit limit, as the tester did), not just on a normal machine — otherwise it will pass even though the defect is still there.
ws2.program: mukhya() { kosh k[4]; chakra i = 0 tak 10000000 { kosh_kship(k, 1) }; likha(kosh_gan(k)) } — 6 lines, 10M pushes (~80 MB), under a 64 MB budget. chakra ... tak 10000000 is inclusive, so it pushes 10,000,001 times (10,000,001 elements, ~80 MB). It is a kosh-growth OOM program (not a nirmmita OOM — see below), and it exhausts a small budget quickly (after ~8M pushes, ~0.1 s, well under the 10M in the loop). Delivered as r133_ws_r133_oom_small.sm.
ws2.refuse_or_crash: It refuses on Linux and crashes on Windows (for the same program, under a small budget/commit limit). It does NOT refuse on both. On Windows (not verified by me running Windows — from the tester's table + the code reading): the tester's table (100M-element kosh, same growth path) shows 64/128/256 MiB -> 0xC0000005, empty output, and 2048 MiB -> exit 0, output 100000000. My 10M-push program is the same growth path (kosh growth, via the arena/region), so under a 64 MiB Job commit limit it should crash the same way (0xC0000005, empty output) — because the failure happens at touch time (arena page-commit via rt_veh, which has no OOM handling, WS1 #5), not at allocation time (region mmap, which would refuse).
ws2.why_kosh_growth_not_nirmmita: A nirmmita OOM (e.g. vitti p = nirmmita(100000000) (100 MB) under a 64 MB budget — one call, no loop) would be even smaller (one allocation, not millions of pushes), but it triggers a DIFFERENT path: nirmmita returns 0 on failure (on both platforms, via the normalisation, WS1 #4), and the program must check it — if it does not check, it will use 0 as a pointer (crash on both platforms, or print 0 if it just prints the pointer). It would NOT trigger the kosh growth message (kosh vardhayitum smritih na labdha), and it would NOT demonstrate the Windows crash in the growth path (the brief's defect). So for WS2 (the kosh growth OOM path, the one that refuses on Linux and crashes on Windows), a kosh-growth program is the right smallest program. A nirmmita OOM program would test a different (also worth testing, but different) path, and I note it here so it is not confused with this one.

ws3.clears: Nothing. Neither load_file (on failure) nor restore_prev_file nor output_append clears the editor or the output pane. The only thing that changes on a refused load is: the warning is appended to the output pane, and current_file is restored to prev_file (so the title is correct).
ws3.fix_for_claude: In load_file's .too_big (and .fail) path (windows/gui/sutram_gui.asm:2627, specifically the .too_big branch at lines 2668-2670), or in the callers after a failed load, CLEAR the output pane (e.g. SetWindowText(h_output, '') or EM_SETSEL (0,-1) + EM_REPLACESEL ('')) BEFORE appending the warning, so the pane shows ONLY the warning (not the stale output above it). Do NOT clear the editor (that would discard the student's work — the previous file is still the current file). The function to change is load_file (line 2627, .too_big at 2668-2670) and/or output_append (line 2818, to take a 'clear first' flag, or to be preceded by a clear in the failure path).
ws3.function_and_line: load_file, windows/gui/sutram_gui.asm:2627. The line that leaves the stale output is the .too_big branch (lines 2668-2670): PTR rcx,msg_input_large; call output_append (then falls through to .fail, returns 0). msg_input_large (line 295) is '[patram atibrihat; sampadaka-seema 64 KiB]' (the file is too large; editor limit 64 KiB). MAX_EDIT is 65534 (line 107: %define MAX_EDIT 65534 — not 65536; the buffer is 65536 bytes, but the limit is 65534, leaving room for the NUL terminator). The 70,422-byte example exceeds 65534, so it is refused. output_append (line 2818, 'Append a string to output control without moving existing user text') does EM_SETSEL (-1,-1) then EM_REPLACESEL (insert at the end) — it does NOT clear the output first (no EM_SETSEL (0,-1) + EM_REPLACESEL (''), no SetWindowText(h_output, '')). So it APPENDS the warning BELOW the existing (stale) output, in the same output pane, in the same style. The callers (lines 2577 and 2797, the Open dialog handlers) call restore_prev_file on load_file failure (test eax,eax; jnz .end (success); else .restore: call restore_prev_file). restore_prev_file (line 2808, with the comment 'R34: a load was refused (too big, unreadable, not UTF-8): the editor still holds the previous text, so current_file must name the previous file again — else the title would name the refused file and Save would overwrite it with other text') copies prev_file to current_file (so the title names the previous file again) and calls update_title. It does NOT clear the editor and does NOT clear the output pane.
ws3.leaves: The editor showing the previous file, and the output pane showing the previous program's output. The editor showing the previous file is arguably CORRECT — because load_file failed, the previous file is still the current file (and restore_prev_file ensures the title matches it, so the editor and the title agree, and Save will not overwrite the refused file with the previous text). Clearing the editor would be WRONG (it would discard the student's work on the previous file, which is still the current file). The output pane showing the previous program's output is the DEFECT: that output is from running the previous file, and the student just clicked a new file (which was refused, so it was never run) — so the output on screen is NOT from the file they just clicked, and it is NOT current. The warning appended below it ('file too large') is honest, but it is in the same pane and the same style as the stale output above it, so a student can read the stale output and think it is the result of the file they just clicked (or that the program ran and produced that output).
